steps: Bring a pan of water to just below boiling and take it off the heat — weisswurst must never actually boil or the skins split.
Slide the sausages in and let them stand in the hot water for ten to twelve minutes until heated through.
Lift them out with tongs into a warmed bowl with a ladle of the water so they stay hot at the table.
Slit each skin lengthways and peel it back, or suck the sausage out of the casing as the Bavarians do.
Eat with sweet mustard and buttered pretzel, traditionally before midday.

recipes.name: Eggs Benedict
steps: Whisk the two yolks with the lemon juice over a bain-marie until pale and thick, then trickle in the warm melted butter to build a hollandaise; keep it barely warm.
Fry the bacon until the edges crisp and toast the split muffins.
Poach the whole eggs in simmering vinegared water for three minutes and drain them well on a cloth.
Build each half: muffin, bacon, poached egg, then a spoonful of hollandaise poured over so it slides down the sides.
Crack over black pepper and serve immediately — hollandaise waits for nobody.

recipes.name: Kedgeree
steps: Poach the haddock in milk or water for six minutes, then lift it out, discard skin and bones and flake it into big pieces.
Soften the onion in butter, stir in the curry powder and fry a minute until it smells toasted.
Add the washed rice, coat it in the spiced butter, pour in the measured poaching liquid and cook covered until absorbed.
Hard-boil the eggs for eight minutes, cool and quarter them.
Fold the flaked fish through the hot rice off the heat, top with the eggs, parsley and a hard squeeze of lemon.

recipes.name: Bubble and Squeak
steps: Fry the onion in butter until soft and lightly browned at the edges.
Mix in the cold mash and cabbage, season hard with salt and pepper, and press the lot flat into the pan.
Leave it alone over medium heat for eight minutes so a proper brown crust forms underneath — the squeak is the cabbage in the hot fat.
Flip in sections with a fish slice, add a little more butter and crust the second side.
Serve in wedges with brown sauce, or alongside cold roast leftovers.

recipes.name: Welsh Rarebit
steps: Melt the butter, stir in the flour and cook one minute, then whisk in the milk to a thick paste.
Take off the heat and beat in the cheese, mustard and cayenne until it becomes a stiff, glossy mixture.
Toast the bread on both sides so it can carry the topping without going soggy.
Spread the cheese mixture thickly right to the edges and blister it under a hot grill for three minutes until bubbling and freckled brown.

recipes.name: Ulster Fry
steps: Start the sausages in a cold pan over low heat and let them cook slowly for fifteen minutes, turning, so they brown without bursting.
Add the bacon and black pudding to the same pan and cook until the bacon fat is crisp and the pudding has a crust.
Fry the soda farls and potato bread in the rendered fat — this is the part that makes it an Ulster fry rather than any other fry.
Crack the eggs into the pan last and baste them with hot fat until the whites set.
Plate everything at once with strong tea; nothing here is served separately.

recipes.name: Cardamom Buns
steps: Crush the cardamom seeds coarsely in a mortar — pre-ground powder will not give the resinous hit these buns need.
Make a soft enriched dough with warm milk, yeast, flour, half the sugar, half the butter and a third of the cardamom, and prove until doubled.
Roll into a large rectangle, spread with the remaining soft butter, sugar and cardamom, fold in three and cut into strips.
Twist each strip and knot it around two fingers, tucking the end underneath, then prove again for forty minutes.
Bake at 220C for ten to twelve minutes, then brush hot with sugar syrup and scatter pearl sugar.

recipes.name: Karelian Pies
steps: Simmer the rice in the milk with salt, stirring often, for thirty-five minutes until it becomes a thick, sticky porridge, then cool it.
Make a stiff dough of rye flour, water and salt, roll it into very thin ovals — thin enough to read through.
Spoon porridge down the centre of each oval and crimp the long edges up over it, leaving the middle open.
Bake at 250C for fifteen minutes until the rye rims blister and darken, then brush at once with melted butter and cover with a cloth to soften.
Mash the hard-boiled eggs with soft butter and salt and spoon this egg butter over the pies to serve.

recipes.name: Syrniki
steps: Press the farmer's cheese through a sieve so there are no lumps — this is the difference between light syrniki and rubbery ones.
Mix in the egg, sugar, raisins and just enough flour to bring it together; the dough should still be soft.
Shape into thick discs with floured hands and dust the outsides lightly.
Fry in butter over medium-low heat for three to four minutes a side so the middles heat through before the crust burns.
Serve hot with cold sour cream and jam.

recipes.name: Banitsa
steps: Whisk the eggs with the yogurt and baking soda, then crumble in the sirene — the soda makes the custard rise between the layers.
Brush a filo sheet with butter, spread a ladle of the mixture over it and roll it loosely into a rope.
Coil the first rope in the centre of a round tin and wind the rest around it in a spiral.
Pour any remaining egg mixture over the top and brush with the last of the butter.
Bake at 190C for thirty-five minutes until the spiral is deep gold, then rest fifteen minutes before cutting.

recipes.name: Blini with Sour Cream
steps: Whisk both flours with the warm milk and yeast into a loose batter and leave it in a warm place for an hour until pocked with bubbles.
Beat in the egg, melted butter and a good pinch of salt just before cooking.
Drop tablespoons of batter onto a hot buttered pan and cook until the surface is covered in burst bubbles.
Flip and give them another minute, stacking the cooked blini under a cloth to stay soft.
Serve warm with cold sour cream and, if you have it, pickled herring or jam.

recipes.name: Huevos Divorciados
steps: Boil the tomatillos with one chilli, then blend with onion and coriander for the salsa verde and season it.
Char the tomatoes with the second chilli in a dry pan and blend for the salsa roja, then fry each salsa separately in a little oil for five minutes.
Crisp the tortillas lightly and set them on the plate with a ridge of refried beans running down the middle.
Fry the eggs sunny side up and lay one on each tortilla.
Flood one egg with the green salsa and the other with the red so the beans keep them apart.

recipes.name: Molletes
steps: Split the rolls, pull out a little of the crumb to make a trough and butter the cut faces.
Toast them butter-side up under the grill until the edges colour.
Spread the warm refried beans thickly into the trough and blanket with grated cheese.
Grill again until the cheese blisters and slides.
Top with pico de gallo made from the diced tomato, onion, chilli and lime, and eat open-faced.

recipes.name: Gallo Pinto
steps: Fry the onion, pepper and garlic in oil until soft and just starting to catch.
Add the beans together with a few spoons of their black cooking liquor and let it bubble for two minutes so the colour deepens.
Tip in the cold rice and toss hard so every grain takes on the bean liquor and turns speckled — this speckling is what gives the dish its name.
Stir in the Salsa Lizano and cook another three minutes until dry rather than wet.
Finish with chopped coriander and serve with fried sweet plantain on the side.

recipes.name: Baleadas
steps: Work the flour, salt, oil and warm water into a soft dough and rest it thirty minutes so it rolls out without springing back.
Roll each ball into a large thin round and cook on a dry hot comal, about forty seconds a side, until it puffs and freckles.
Keep the cooked tortillas stacked under a cloth so they stay pliable — a stiff tortilla will crack when folded.
Spread warm refried beans over half of each tortilla, drizzle crema and scatter crumbled salty cheese.
Fold in half and eat by hand, adding scrambled egg or avocado if you want it fuller.

recipes.name: Johnny Cakes
steps: Rub the cold butter into the flour, baking powder, sugar and salt until it looks like coarse sand.
Bring it together with just enough milk to make a firm dough and knead briefly — overworking makes them tough.
Rest the dough twenty minutes, then roll into balls and flatten slightly.
Fry in oil at a moderate 160C so they cook through and puff before the outsides brown, turning once, about eight minutes.
Drain and split open while hot to eat with saltfish, cheese or just butter.

recipes.name: Cornmeal Porridge
steps: Slake the cornmeal in a cup of cold water first — dropping dry cornmeal into hot liquid guarantees lumps.
Bring the milk, coconut milk and cinnamon stick to a simmer, then pour in the slaked cornmeal in a thin stream, whisking constantly.
Cook on low for ten minutes, stirring often, until it thickens and loses its raw grain taste.
Sweeten with condensed milk and finish with vanilla and freshly grated nutmeg.

recipes.name: Mangu with Tres Golpes
steps: Boil the peeled plantains in salted water for twenty minutes until a knife slides in easily, keeping a cup of the water.
Mash them hot with butter and enough of the cooking water to give a smooth, heavy purée — never use a blender, it turns gluey.
Soak the sliced red onion in vinegar with a little salt for ten minutes, then wilt it briefly in hot oil.
Fry the three hits separately in the same pan: salami until curled, cheese until crusted, eggs until the edges frill.
Mound the mangu, crown it with the pickled onion and set the salami, cheese and egg around it.

recipes.name: Youtiao with Soy Milk
steps: Mix flour, raising agents, salt and water into a wet dough, oil the surface and refrigerate it overnight — the long rest is what gives the hollow interior.
Roll the cold dough into a strip, cut into fingers and press two together down the middle with a chopstick.
Stretch each pair to about twenty centimetres and lower into oil at 190C.
Turn constantly for ninety seconds until they balloon, twist and turn golden, then drain upright.
Warm the soy milk with a little sugar and serve alongside for dunking, or salty with vinegar and pickle if you prefer it savoury.

recipes.name: Jianbing
steps: Whisk both flours with water to a thin, pourable batter and rest it fifteen minutes.
Pour a ladle onto a hot flat griddle and spread it into a wide thin circle with a wooden spreader or the back of a spoon.
Crack an egg on top, break the yolk and smear it across the setting crepe, then scatter spring onion and coriander so they stick.
Flip the whole crepe, brush the cooked side with sweet bean and chilli sauce, and lay the crisp wonton sheet in the middle.
Fold the sides in over the cracker, fold again into a parcel, cut in half and eat before it softens.

recipes.name: Turnip Cake
steps: Simmer the grated daikon in a little water for fifteen minutes until translucent and collapsed, keeping all the liquid.
Fry the sausage, drained shrimp and shiitake until fragrant and the sausage fat has run.
Mix the rice flour into the hot radish and its liquid to a thick paste, then fold through the fried mixture, white pepper and salt.
Press into an oiled tin and steam for fifty minutes until a skewer comes out clean, then chill completely — warm cake will not slice.
Cut into thick slabs and pan-fry in a little oil until both faces are crisp and golden, serving with chilli or oyster sauce.

recipes.name: Tamagoyaki
steps: Beat the eggs with the dashi, soy, mirin and sugar, then strain the mixture to remove the chalazae so the roll is smooth.
Heat a rectangular tamagoyaki pan over low-medium heat and wipe it with oil on a folded paper towel.
Pour in a thin layer, pop any bubbles, and when it is just set on top roll it away from you into a log at one end of the pan.
Oil the empty pan, pour the next layer under and around the rolled log, and roll back over it; repeat until the batter is used.
Turn the roll out onto a bamboo mat, shape it while hot, cool a minute and cut into thick slices.

recipes.name: Tamago Kake Gohan
steps: Fill a bowl with rice straight from the pot — it must be hot enough to lightly cook the egg as you stir.
Crack in the egg, or use only the yolk for a richer bowl, and add the soy sauce.
Beat the egg through the rice quickly with chopsticks until every grain is coated and the mixture turns glossy and pale.
Top with spring onion and shredded nori and eat immediately, while it is still steaming.

recipes.name: Korean Egg Toast
steps: Beat the eggs with the shredded cabbage, carrot, spring onion and salt into a loose vegetable batter.
Fry the bread in plenty of butter on a flat pan until both sides are gold and soaked — this is street food, do not be shy with the butter.
Pour the egg mixture into the same pan as a rough rectangle, cook until set, then fold the edges in to match the size of the bread.
Sit the egg patty on a slice, sprinkle over the sugar — the sweet-salty jolt is the point — and squiggle on ketchup.
Close the sandwich, press it down, cut in half and wrap in paper to eat walking.

recipes.name: Banh Cuon
steps: Whisk the rice flour and tapioca starch with water and a little oil into a very thin batter and rest it at least two hours.
Fry the minced pork with chopped wood ear mushroom, shallot, fish sauce and pepper until dry and fragrant.
Stretch muslin over a pot of boiling water, ladle a thin film of batter over it, cover and steam forty seconds until the sheet turns translucent.
Lift the sheet onto an oiled tray with a flat stick, lay a spoon of pork along one edge and roll it up loosely.
Serve the rolls scattered with crisp fried shallots, blanched bean sprouts and herbs, with nuoc cham of fish sauce, lime, sugar and chilli to pour over.

recipes.name: Khao Tom
steps: Fry the sliced garlic in oil until pale gold and lift it out to drain — this crisp garlic and its oil go over the top at the end.
Season the minced pork with a little fish sauce and white pepper and roll it into small balls or leave it loose.
Bring the stock to a boil with half the ginger, drop in the pork and simmer three minutes until just cooked.
Add the cooked rice and simmer a further five minutes; the grains should stay whole and swimming, not break down like congee.
Season with fish sauce, ladle out and finish with the fried garlic and its oil, raw ginger, coriander and spring onion.

recipes.name: Bubur Ayam
steps: Poach the chicken with lemongrass, ginger and salt for twenty minutes, then lift it out, shred the meat and keep the broth.
Cook the washed rice in that broth with the turmeric on a low flame for thirty minutes, stirring often and adding water until it collapses into a soft porridge.
Toss the shredded chicken in a pan with kecap manis and a little of its poaching liquid until glazed.
Ladle the porridge into bowls and pile the sweet-soy chicken in the centre.
Top with fried shallots, fried peanuts, spring onion, crackers and a spoon of sambal at the side.

recipes.name: Tapsilog
steps: Marinate the sliced beef overnight in soy sauce, calamansi, crushed garlic, brown sugar and black pepper.
Fry sliced garlic in oil until golden, drain it, then toss the cold rice in the garlic oil with salt to make sinangag.
Fry the drained tapa in a hot pan in a single layer so it caramelises rather than stews, about three minutes a side.
Fry the eggs sunny side up with crisp lacy edges.
Plate the three components side by side and serve with spiced vinegar for dipping the beef.

recipes.name: Champorado
steps: Rinse the glutinous rice and simmer it in the water, stirring often so it does not stick, until the grains swell and burst.
Drop in the tablea and stir until they dissolve completely and the porridge turns deep brown and thick.
Sweeten with sugar and a pinch of salt, and loosen with more hot water if it stiffens past a spoonable consistency.
Serve hot with a swirl of evaporated milk poured on at the table, traditionally alongside salted dried fish.

recipes.name: Pandesal
steps: Mix the warm milk, yeast and sugar, then work in the flour, salt and softened butter and knead ten minutes to a smooth elastic dough.
Prove until doubled, knock back and roll into a log, then cut the log into pieces with a scraper so each roll has two cut faces.
Roll the cut pieces in fine breadcrumbs and set them cut-side up on a tray with room to spread.
Prove a second time for thirty minutes until light and puffy.
Bake at 190C for fifteen minutes until pale gold — pandesal should stay soft, not crusty — and eat warm with butter or cheese.

recipes.name: Chechebsa
steps: Mix the flour with salt and water into a soft dough and roll it thin enough to cook through quickly.
Cook the flatbread on a dry hot griddle for two minutes a side until it is dry and lightly blistered.
Tear or cut it into small pieces straight in the pan while still hot.
Melt the niter kibbeh, stir in the berbere off the heat, and toss the torn bread through until every piece is coated red and glossy.
Drizzle with honey and serve with plain yogurt to cool the chilli.

recipes.name: Firfir
steps: Dry-fry the chopped onion in a pan with no oil until it collapses and starts to stick — this slow sweating is the base of nearly every Ethiopian sauce.
Add the oil and garlic, then the berbere, and fry a minute so the spice loses its rawness.
Stir in the tomatoes and a splash of water and cook down to a thick red sauce.
Tear the day-old injera into strips and fold them through the sauce off the heat until they have drunk it up but still hold their shape.
Finish with ground cardamom and serve with fresh injera and green chilli.

recipes.name: Akara
steps: Soak the black-eyed peas for two hours, then rub them between your palms in water to slip off the skins and float them away.
Blend the peeled peas with the onion, chilli and pepper using as little water as possible into a thick paste.
Whisk the paste hard with a wooden spoon for several minutes until it lightens and holds air — this is what makes akara puff instead of sink.
Season with salt only at the end, then drop spoonfuls into oil at 175C.
Fry six to eight minutes, turning, until deep brown and hollow-sounding, and drain; eat with pap or bread.

recipes.name: Msemen
steps: Knead the flour, half the semolina, salt and warm water into a very soft, almost sticky dough and rest it fifteen minutes under oil.
Oil your hands and the worktop, take a ball of dough and stretch it outwards until it is nearly transparent — tears are fine, thickness is not.
Brush the sheet with melted butter and dust with the remaining semolina, then fold the sides to the middle and the ends over to make a square packet.
Rest the squares ten minutes, flatten each gently and cook on a hot griddle, pressing with a spatula, until both sides are crisp and layered.
Serve hot with honey and mint tea, or stuffed with onion and pepper for a savoury version.

recipes.name: Safed Maas
steps: Boil the onions with cardamom and mace, then grind to a pale paste with no browning at all.
Sear the mutton in ghee over low heat so it stays white, then add the onion paste and cook covered for twenty minutes.
Take the pan off the heat, whisk in the curd a spoon at a time so it does not split, then simmer until the mutton is tender.
Finish with cashew paste and cream, season with white pepper, and rest the curry ten minutes before serving with roti.

recipes.name: Junglee Maas
steps: Soak the whole red chillies in warm water for twenty minutes, then tear them roughly without grinding.
Heat the ghee in a heavy pot, throw in the crushed garlic and torn chillies and let them bloom for a minute.
Add the mutton and salt, cover, and cook on a low fire in its own juices, adding a splash of water only when it catches.
Cook until the ghee separates and clings red to the meat, with almost no gravy left in the pot.

recipes.name: Papad ki Sabzi
steps: Whisk the curd with gram flour, turmeric and chilli powder and a cup of water until completely lump free.
Temper cumin and asafoetida in ghee, then pour in the curd mixture and stir continuously until it comes to a boil.
Simmer eight minutes so the gram flour loses its raw taste and the gravy thickens.
Break the papads into large pieces, slide them in, switch off after one minute and serve at once before they soften completely.

recipes.name: Mangodi ki Sabzi
steps: Fry the dried mangodi in hot mustard oil until they turn a deep nut brown, then lift them out.
In the same oil temper cumin and asafoetida, add the tomatoes and dry spices and cook to a thick masala.
Lower the heat, stir in the curd, then return the mangodi with two cups of water.
Simmer twenty minutes until the mangodi swell and turn soft and the gravy thickens around them.

recipes.name: Doh Khleh
steps: Boil the pork belly in salted water with a slice of ginger until just tender, about thirty minutes.
Cool the meat completely and cut it into small even cubes so it holds shape when tossed.
Toss the pork with sliced onion, ginger, slit green chillies and plenty of lemon juice.
Season with salt, fold through torn coriander and serve at room temperature the same day.

recipes.name: Doh Neiiong
steps: Dry roast the black sesame seeds until they crackle and smell nutty, then grind to a coarse dark paste.
Fry the onion and ginger garlic paste, add the pork with turmeric and salt and brown it well.
Add a cup of water, cover and simmer until the pork is soft and the fat has rendered out.
Stir in the sesame paste and slit chillies and cook ten more minutes until the gravy turns thick, black and glossy.

recipes.name: Smoked Pork with Axone
steps: Rinse the smoked pork in hot water to soften it and wash off surface ash, then cut into thick chunks.
Pound the axone with garlic, ginger and the raja mircha into a rough paste.
Boil the pork in just enough water for twenty minutes, then stir in the axone paste and salt.
Add the greens, simmer uncovered until the water reduces to a clinging gravy and the kitchen smells sharply fermented.

recipes.name: Galho
steps: Boil the smoked pork with crushed garlic and the dried chilli until the meat begins to loosen from the bone.
Add the washed rice and lentils with plenty of water and cook, stirring, until everything collapses into a thick porridge.
Fold in the chopped mustard greens in the last five minutes so they stay bright.
Season with salt, loosen with hot water to a spoonable consistency and serve steaming in bowls.

recipes.name: Eromba
steps: Boil the potatoes and beans together until very soft and drain them well.
Roast the ngari over an open flame until it smells strong, and soak the dried chillies in hot water.
Pound the chillies and ngari to a paste, then mash everything together with the vegetables by hand or in a mortar.
Work in chopped chives and coriander with salt and serve at room temperature alongside plain rice.

recipes.name: Chamthong
steps: Bring water to the boil with the roasted ngari, sliced onion and salt to build a clear savoury broth.
Add the hardest vegetables first and the soft ones a few minutes later so nothing overcooks.
Drop in slit green chillies and simmer just until everything is tender but still holding shape.
Finish with a large handful of chopped chives off the heat and ladle over rice.

recipes.name: Phagshapa

ingredients.name: Pork belly with fat, in strips

steps: Render the pork strips slowly in a dry pan so the fat melts out and the strips turn translucent.
Add sliced ginger and whole dried chillies torn in half and fry until the chillies darken.
Tip in the radish batons with a splash of water, cover and steam until they turn glassy but still snap.
Season with salt and cook uncovered for a few minutes so the liquid clings to the pork and radish.

recipes.name: Chakhwi
steps: Boil the pork with crushed garlic, turmeric and salt until half cooked, skimming the froth.
Rinse the bamboo shoot once to tame its sourness, then add it with the berma and green papaya.
Simmer covered on a low flame until the papaya melts and thickens the broth on its own.
Crush in the green chillies at the end and serve loose and soupy over rice.

recipes.name: Assamese Xaak Bhaji
steps: Wash the greens in several changes of water and chop them coarsely with their tender stalks.
Heat mustard oil to smoking, then drop the heat and crackle panch phoron with crushed garlic and dried chilli.
Add the greens in handfuls, letting each lot wilt before the next goes in.
Salt at the very end and cook uncovered a minute more so the water evaporates and the greens stay green.

recipes.name: Dhuska
steps: Soak the rice and chana dal together for four hours, then grind to a thick batter with ginger and green chilli.
Beat in turmeric and salt and rest the batter half an hour so it aerates slightly.
Drop ladlefuls into hot oil and spoon oil over the top so each dhuska puffs into a golden disc.
Drain on paper and serve hot with ghugni or aloo chokha.

recipes.name: Chicken Taash
steps: Beat the chicken slices flat between sheets so they cook fast and stay thin as a playing card.
Marinate them in curd, ginger garlic paste, chilli powder and salt for at least an hour.
Sear the slices in smoking mustard oil on a hot tawa, pressing them down, until charred at the edges.
Toss with sliced raw onion and a squeeze of lime and serve straight off the pan.

recipes.name: Dalma
steps: Boil the toor dal with turmeric and the cubed vegetables until both are soft but the vegetables still hold.
Stir in grated coconut and salt and simmer so the dal thickens around the vegetables.
Temper panch phoron and a dried chilli in ghee and pour it in sizzling.
Finish with roasted cumin powder crushed by hand, which is what makes dalma taste like dalma.

recipes.name: Santula
steps: Cut all the vegetables into long fingers of roughly the same size so they cook evenly.
Boil them with turmeric, salt and slit green chillies in barely enough water to cover.
When the water has almost gone, mash a few pieces lightly against the pan to thicken the dish.
Pour over a tempering of panch phoron and crushed garlic in mustard oil and stir once before serving.

recipes.name: Macha Besara
steps: Rub the fish steaks with turmeric and salt and shallow fry them briefly in mustard oil, then set aside.
Grind mustard seeds with garlic and a little water into a smooth pungent paste and let it stand.
Temper cumin in the same oil, add the tomato, then the mustard paste, and cook gently without letting it boil hard or it turns bitter.
Slide the fish back in with a cup of water and simmer eight minutes until the gravy coats the pieces.

recipes.name: Pakhala Bhata
steps: Cover the cooled cooked rice with water and leave it overnight, or at least six hours, to ferment gently.
Next day beat in the curd with salt so the liquid turns cloudy and mildly sour.
Temper mustard seeds and curry leaves in a spoon of oil and stir it through with grated ginger and slit chilli.
Serve cold in deep bowls with fried badi, roasted brinjal and a wedge of lime.

recipes.name: Chana Dal Bafauri
steps: Soak the chana dal four hours, drain it fully and grind coarse with ginger and green chilli, using no water.
Mix in chopped coriander, ajwain and salt and beat the batter with your hand until it feels light.
Shape into small balls and steam them for fifteen minutes until a skewer comes out clean.
Cool slightly so they firm up and serve with green chutney; they need no frying at all.

recipes.name: Aamat
steps: Pressure cook the toor dal with turmeric until it collapses completely.
Boil the bamboo shoot separately in salted water for ten minutes and discard that water to soften its bite.
Add the bamboo shoot, drumstick and tamarind pulp to the dal and simmer until the drumsticks are tender.
Pour over a hot tempering of garlic and dried chillies and eat with coarse rice.

recipes.name: Kafuli
steps: Blanch the mixed greens briefly, then grind them coarse so the dish keeps its texture.
Whisk rice flour into the curd until smooth, which is what thickens kafuli without any cream.
Fry garlic and green chilli in ghee, add the ground greens and cook five minutes.
Lower the flame, stir in the curd slurry and simmer gently until the pan smells nutty and the greens turn glossy.

recipes.name: Chainsoo
steps: Dry roast the whole black urad on a griddle until it smells toasted, then grind it to a coarse meal.
Fry ginger and garlic in mustard oil, add the ground dal and roast it in the oil for a few minutes.
Pour in hot water a little at a time, whisking so no lumps form, then cook long and slow in an iron kadhai.
Simmer for at least half an hour until thick, dark and smoky, and finish with a spoon of ghee.

recipes.name: Chana Madra
steps: Boil the soaked chickpeas with salt until soft but not falling apart, and keep the cooking water.
Bloom whole cloves, cardamom and cinnamon in ghee until fragrant, then add cashews and raisins.
Take the pan off the heat and whisk in the curd slowly so it never splits, then return it on the lowest flame.
Add the chickpeas and cook uncovered for twenty minutes, stirring often, until the yogurt gravy thickens and turns glossy.

recipes.name: Siddu
steps: Knead a soft wheat dough with yeast and warm water and let it rise for at least four hours until spongy.
Roast the walnuts and poppy seeds, then pound them with green chilli and salt into a coarse stuffing.
Roll out portions of dough, place the filling in the centre and fold into a half moon, sealing the edge well.
Steam for twenty minutes until the siddu is puffed and springy, and serve hot with melted ghee or mint chutney.

recipes.name: Seyal Gosht
steps: Grind coriander, mint, green chilli and garlic into a thick green masala with no water.
Brown the onions in oil, add the tomatoes and cook them down until the oil separates.
Add the mutton and the green masala together and bhuno on a high flame for ten minutes so the herbs cook into the meat.
Cover and cook on low with minimal water until the mutton is tender and the gravy is dark green and clinging.

recipes.name: Sindhi Bhee Patata
steps: Scrub the lotus stem well, slice it into rounds and parboil with salt and turmeric until it loses its raw crunch.
Fry the onion until soft, add tomato, coriander powder and chilli powder and cook to a thick masala.
Add the potato and drained lotus stem and toss so every piece is coated.
Cover and cook on low until the potato is done, then finish with amchur and coriander leaves for a dry tangy sabzi.

recipes.name: Sungtachi Kodi
steps: Roast the grated coconut with half the sliced onion in a dry pan until it turns golden brown and smells toasted.
Grind that to a fine paste with Malvani masala and a little water.
Fry the remaining onion in coconut oil, add the ground paste and cook until the oil rises to the surface.
Slide in the prawns with the kokum and a cup of water and simmer only five minutes so they stay plump.

recipes.name: Tisrya Masala
steps: Scrub the clams hard under running water and discard any that stay open when tapped.
Steam them in a covered pan with no water until they open, then keep the half shells and their liquor.
Fry chopped onion and garlic till brown, add chilli powder and grated coconut and roast a few minutes.
Toss the clams back in with their liquor, cook two minutes so the masala clings, and finish with coriander.

recipes.name: Kombdi Vade
steps: Roast coconut with onion and whole spices, grind to the dark vatan paste that gives Malvani curry its colour.
Cook the chicken with the vatan and Malvani masala until the gravy is thin, red and fiercely aromatic.
For the vade, mix rice, wheat and urad flours with black pepper and salt and knead a stiff dough with hot water.
Pat the dough into small thick discs, prick them, and deep fry until puffed; serve two vade to a bowl of curry.

recipes.name: Pandi Curry
steps: Cook the pork in a heavy pot with turmeric, salt and no added water so it releases its own fat and juices.
Dry roast coriander, cumin, pepper and mustard seeds and grind them fresh with ginger and garlic.
Fry the onions in the rendered pork fat, add the ground spice and roast it until very dark.
Return the pork, simmer covered for an hour, then stir in the kachampuli at the end for its sharp black sourness.

recipes.name: Koli Barthad
steps: Roast coriander seeds and peppercorns separately, then crush them coarse so you still bite into the pepper.
Brown the sliced onions deeply in coconut oil with curry leaves.
Add the chicken with turmeric and salt, cover and cook in its own moisture until nearly done.
Stir in the crushed spice mix and fry uncovered on high heat until the pieces are dry, dark and coated.

recipes.name: Bangude Pulimunchi
steps: Roast the Byadgi chillies, coriander, cumin and peppercorns lightly in a dry pan.
Grind them with tamarind, garlic and turmeric into a smooth fiery red paste using very little water.
Bring the paste to a boil in coconut oil with water and salt and cook ten minutes until the raw chilli smell goes.
Slip in the mackerel, simmer eight minutes without stirring, and rest an hour before eating so the sourness soaks in.

recipes.name: Golichina Mamsam
steps: Pressure cook the mutton with ginger garlic paste, turmeric and salt until soft, keeping the stock.
Brown the sliced onions in oil with curry leaves until they turn deep golden.
Add the cooked mutton with chilli powder and fry on high heat, adding the stock a spoon at a time.
Keep frying until every drop has gone and the pieces are dark and dry, then finish with crushed pepper.

recipes.name: Natu Kodi Pulusu
steps: Marinate the country chicken in turmeric, salt and chilli powder for half an hour; it needs longer cooking than broiler.
Fry onions with curry leaves in sesame oil until soft, add ginger garlic and the powdered spices.
Add the chicken and bhuno until it seizes and colours, then pour in three cups of water and simmer covered for forty minutes.
Stir in the tamarind pulp and cook fifteen minutes more so the pulusu turns thin, sour and hot.

recipes.name: Mirchi ka Salan
steps: Slit the green chillies, scrape out most seeds and shallow fry them until blistered, then set aside.
Dry roast peanuts, sesame and dry coconut, cool, and grind with fried onion into a thick brown paste.
Cook the paste in oil with chilli powder and turmeric until the oil floats on top.
Add tamarind pulp and water, simmer twenty minutes, then slide in the chillies and cook five minutes more.

recipes.name: Dalcha
steps: Cook the mutton with ginger garlic paste, turmeric and salt until tender, keeping the stock.
Boil the chana dal separately with bottle gourd until both are completely soft, then mash lightly.
Combine dal and mutton with its stock, add tamarind pulp and simmer twenty minutes so the flavours marry.
Finish with a tempering of curry leaves, dried chilli and sliced onion fried in ghee; serve with bagara rice.

recipes.name: Saoji Chicken
steps: Dry roast dry coconut, poppy seeds, stone flower and whole spices until dark and smoky.
Brown the onions separately until nearly burnt, then grind everything together into a black paste.
Fry the paste in oil with chilli powder until the oil pools red at the edges, which takes patience.
Add the chicken, sear it in the masala, then add hot water and simmer until the gravy is thin, oily and searingly hot.

recipes.name: Patodi Rassa
steps: Cook gram flour with water, turmeric and salt, stirring hard, until it thickens like a dough and leaves the pan.
Spread it on a greased plate, smooth the top, cool and cut into diamonds; these are the patodi.
For the rassa, roast onion, dry coconut and peanuts, grind to a paste and fry with kanda lasun masala until oil separates.
Add hot water to make a thin fiery gravy, simmer ten minutes, and slide the patodi in just before serving.

recipes.name: Kakori Kebab
steps: Grind the mince a second time with mutton fat until it is smooth as a paste, then mix in raw papaya paste and rest it two hours.
Work in khoya, fried onion paste, nut powder and the fine Awadhi spice mix, kneading until sticky.
Smoke the mixture with a live coal and ghee under a covered bowl for ten minutes.
Wrap the mince around wet skewers with oiled hands and grill over charcoal, basting with ghee, until just set and impossibly soft.

recipes.name: Murgh Musallam
steps: Prick the whole chicken all over and marinate it overnight in curd, ginger garlic, chilli and garam masala.
Cook the keema with spices, cool, and stuff it into the cavity along with the boiled eggs, then truss the bird.
Brown the chicken in ghee on all sides, then set it in a heavy pot with the fried onion and cashew paste and its marinade.
Seal the lid with dough and cook on dum over a very low flame for an hour, finishing with saffron milk and kewra.

recipes.name: Kathal ki Biryani
steps: Rub your hands with oil before cutting the jackfruit, then deep fry the cubes until golden so they hold their shape.
Marinate the fried jackfruit in curd, fried onions, ginger garlic and biryani masala for an hour.
Parboil the basmati with whole spices until seventy percent done and drain it well.
Layer jackfruit and rice in a heavy pot, pour over saffron milk and ghee, seal the lid and cook on dum for twenty five minutes.

recipes.name: Dabba Gosht

ingredients.name: Green chutney of coriander and mint

steps: Cook the mutton with onion, ginger garlic and green chutney until tender and almost dry.
Soak the breadcrumbs in milk and beat with the eggs and cashew paste into a loose custard.
Spread the mutton in a greased dish, pour the egg mixture over it and scatter grated cheese on top.
Bake at 180C for thirty five minutes until set, puffed and browned, then rest before cutting into squares.

recipes.name: Dhansak
steps: Pressure cook the mixed lentils with pumpkin, brinjal and fenugreek leaves until everything is falling apart, then blend smooth.
Separately brown the mutton with onions, ginger garlic and dhansak masala.
Combine the meat with the lentil puree and tamarind and simmer for half an hour so it thickens to a heavy gravy.
Serve with brown rice cooked with caramelised sugar and a kachumber of onion and lime.

recipes.name: Patra ni Machhi
steps: Grind coconut, coriander, green chilli, cumin, sugar and lime juice into a thick bright green chutney.
Coat the fish fillets generously on both sides and let them sit twenty minutes.
Soften the banana leaves over a flame, wrap each fillet into a neat parcel and tie with string.
Steam the parcels for twelve to fifteen minutes and open them at the table so the perfume escapes there.

recipes.name: Salli Boti
steps: Brown the onions well, add ginger garlic and the mutton and sear it hard.
Add tomatoes, chilli and dhansak or garam masala and cook until the fat separates.
Stir in jaggery, vinegar and the dried apricots and simmer covered until the mutton is soft and the gravy is sweet and sour.
Fry potato straws in hot oil until crisp, salt them, and pile them over the curry at the moment of serving.

recipes.name: Berry Pulao
steps: Cook the chicken with fried onions, curd and mild spices into a thick almost dry masala.
Soak the barberries in warm water for ten minutes, drain, and toss them in butter with a little sugar until they plump.
Boil the basmati with whole spices until just done, drain and spread it out so the grains stay separate.
Layer the rice over the chicken, steam on low ten minutes, then fold through the barberries and fried cashews at the table.

recipes.name: Railway Mutton Curry
steps: Fry the onions with curry leaves until soft, add ginger garlic and the curry powder and cook off the raw smell.
Brown the mutton in the masala, then add water and simmer covered for an hour until nearly tender.
Add the potatoes and tamarind pulp and cook until the potatoes are soft enough to break with a spoon.
Stir in the coconut milk and warm through without boiling, so the curry stays thin, mild and travels well.

recipes.name: Bene Israel Chicken Curry
steps: Roast coriander and cumin seeds with dried chilli and grind them into the household masala; no dairy goes anywhere near this dish.
Fry the onions in oil until translucent, add ginger garlic and the ground masala and cook until fragrant.
Add the chicken with salt and turmeric and let it brown in the masala for ten minutes.
Pour in coconut milk and tamarind, simmer gently until the chicken is cooked, and finish with slit chillies and coriander leaves.

recipes.name: Mulligatawny Soup
steps: Simmer the chicken with a bay leaf to make a light stock, then lift out the meat and shred it.
Cook the masoor dal in that stock with curry powder and crushed pepper until it dissolves completely.
Blend the soup smooth, return the shredded chicken and loosen with coconut milk.
Season with lemon juice and salt and ladle over a spoon of hot rice in each bowl.

recipes.name: Shui Zhu Beef
steps: Slice the beef paper-thin across the grain and massage it with cornflour, soy and a little water until slippery.
Blanch the bean sprouts and cabbage and lay them in the bottom of a deep serving bowl.
Fry the doubanjiang in oil, add stock, bring to a boil and poach the beef slices for barely a minute before tipping it all over the vegetables.
Heap chopped dried chilli, garlic and Sichuan pepper on top and pour smoking-hot oil over so it crackles.

recipes.name: Yu Xiang Eggplant
steps: Cut the eggplant into thick batons and shallow-fry until collapsed and golden, then drain.
Fry the doubanjiang with garlic and ginger in a spoon of oil until fragrant and deep red.
Stir in vinegar, sugar, soy and a splash of water to build the sweet-sour-spicy sauce.
Return the eggplant, simmer two minutes and thicken with a cornflour slurry.

recipes.name: Dry Fried Green Beans
steps: Blister the trimmed beans in a lightly oiled wok until the skins wrinkle and char in patches.
Remove the beans and fry the dried chillies and Sichuan peppercorns until they smell toasty.
Add garlic and the chopped preserved mustard greens and fry for a minute.
Return the beans with soy sauce and toss until dry and glossy.

recipes.name: Red Braised Pork Belly
steps: Blanch the cubed pork belly briefly, then drain and pat it dry.
Melt the rock sugar in a little oil until it turns amber and coat the pork in the caramel.
Add wine, dark soy, ginger, star anise and chillies with water to just cover.
Braise covered for an hour, then uncover and reduce until the sauce clings to each piece.

recipes.name: Steamed Fish with Ginger and Scallion
recipes.hindi: स्टीम्ड फिश विद जिंजर एंड स्कैलियन
steps: Score the cleaned fish and lay it on ginger slices in a heatproof plate.
Steam over rapidly boiling water for about ten minutes until the flesh flakes at the bone.
Pour off the cloudy steaming liquid and scatter fine ginger and scallion shreds over the top.
Heat the oil until it smokes, pour it over the aromatics, then finish with warmed soy and sugar.

recipes.name: Salt and Pepper Tofu
steps: Press the tofu dry, cube it and toss in cornflour seasoned with salt and white pepper.
Deep-fry in batches until the crust is pale gold and crisp, then drain on paper.
In a near-dry wok flash-fry the garlic, chilli and spring onion whites for thirty seconds.
Return the tofu, dust with more salt and pepper and toss off the heat so the crust stays crisp.

recipes.name: Buddha's Delight
steps: Soak the shiitake, wood ear and bean curd sticks separately until soft, saving the mushroom water.
Fry the ginger and mashed fermented bean curd in oil until fragrant.
Add cabbage, mushrooms, wood ear and bean curd sticks with the mushroom liquid and soy, then simmer covered for twenty minutes.
Slide in the soaked glass noodles at the end and cook until they turn clear.

recipes.name: Scallion Oil Noodles
steps: Cut the spring onions into lengths and fry them slowly in plenty of oil until deep brown and brittle.
Lift out the crisp scallions and keep the fragrant oil.
Dissolve the sugar in both soy sauces and warm briefly with a spoon of the scallion oil.
Boil the noodles, drain, and toss them hot with the sauce, the scallion oil and the crisp scallions.

recipes.name: Big Plate Chicken
steps: Brown the chicken pieces hard in oil, then add rock sugar, dried chillies, Sichuan pepper and star anise.
Stir in the doubanjiang and enough water to half-cover, then simmer for twenty minutes.
Add chunked potatoes and cook until they start to break down and thicken the gravy.
Fold in the peppers, then tip the whole panful over freshly boiled belt noodles.

recipes.name: Xinjiang Cumin Lamb Skewers
steps: Cut the lamb and its fat into thumbnail cubes and thread them alternately onto flat skewers.
Marinate briefly with grated onion, salt and a spoon of oil.
Grill over hot charcoal, turning constantly so the fat renders and flares.
Shower with coarsely crushed cumin and chilli flakes in the last minute over the coals.

recipes.name: Di San Xian
steps: Fry the potato wedges in hot oil until golden at the edges, then lift them out.
Fry the eggplant chunks in the same oil until soft and browned through.
Flash-fry the peppers and garlic, then return the potato and eggplant to the wok.
Splash in soy, sugar and a cornflour slurry and toss until everything is coated in glossy sauce.

recipes.name: Crossing the Bridge Noodles
steps: Simmer the chicken with ginger for an hour to make a clear, strongly flavoured broth.
Slice the pork and chicken breast paper-thin and arrange them raw on a plate with chives and sprouts.
Pour the boiling broth into a deep pre-heated bowl with a film of chicken fat on top to hold the heat.
Slide in the raw meats and quail eggs to poach in the broth, then add the cooked rice noodles.

recipes.name: Tomato and Egg Stir Fry
steps: Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt and a splash of water until frothy.
Scramble them in hot oil until just set in large soft curds, then lift them out.
Cook the tomato wedges in the same wok with the sugar until they slump into a loose sauce.
Return the egg, season with soy and finish with sesame oil and spring onion.

recipes.name: Lu Rou Fan
steps: Hand-chop the pork belly into small dice rather than mincing it, keeping fat and lean together.
Render the pork in a dry pot until the fat runs and the edges brown.
Add fried shallots, dark soy, rock sugar, wine and five spice with water to cover and simmer for an hour.
Spoon the glossy pork and its sauce over hot rice with a halved braised egg.

recipes.name: Three Cup Chicken
steps: Fry the ginger slices in sesame oil until the edges curl and dry out.
Add whole garlic cloves and the chicken pieces and brown them all over.
Pour in equal cups of rice wine and soy sauce with rock sugar and simmer uncovered until syrupy.
Kill the heat and stir through a huge handful of Thai basil so it wilts in the residual steam.

recipes.name: Oyakodon
steps: Simmer sliced onion in dashi, soy and mirin in a small shallow pan.
Add the bite-sized chicken thigh and poach until just cooked through.
Pour the beaten egg over in two additions and cover so it sets soft and barely wobbling.
Slide the whole thing onto a bowl of hot rice and scatter with mitsuba.

recipes.name: Sukiyaki
steps: Rub a heavy iron pan with beef fat and sear a few slices of beef in it.
Sprinkle over the sugar and pour in soy and mirin to make the warishita broth.
Arrange cabbage, mushrooms, tofu and shirataki around the pan and let it all simmer at the table.
Dip each hot piece into a bowl of beaten raw egg before eating.

recipes.name: Nikujaga
steps: Fry the beef slices and onion in a little oil until the meat loses its raw colour.
Add chunked potato and carrot and turn them through the fat.
Pour in the dashi with soy, mirin and sugar and lay a drop-lid directly on the surface.
Simmer gently for twenty-five minutes until the potatoes are soft and most of the liquid has gone.

recipes.name: Agedashi Tofu
steps: Drain the tofu under a weight for twenty minutes, then cut it into thick blocks.
Warm the kombu and shiitake dashi with soy and mirin to make a light tsuyu broth.
Dust the tofu all over in potato starch and fry at high heat until the coating is pale and crisp.
Sit the tofu in shallow broth and top with grated daikon, ginger and scallion.

recipes.name: Doenjang Jjigae
steps: Simmer dried anchovies and kombu in water for ten minutes, then strain for a clean stock.
Whisk the doenjang into the stock and bring it to a rolling boil.
Add the diced potato and courgette and cook until the potato is tender.
Slide in cubed tofu with garlic and chilli flakes and boil hard for two more minutes.

recipes.name: Sundubu Jjigae
steps: Bloom the gochugaru in hot sesame oil with garlic in an earthenware pot until the oil turns red.
Add the anchovy stock and the clams and boil until the shells open.
Spoon in the soft tofu in large curds without breaking it up too much.
Crack an egg into the bubbling stew and serve it straight from the pot.

recipes.name: Bossam
steps: Simmer the whole slab of pork belly with doenjang, ginger, garlic and a bay leaf for around ninety minutes.
Rest the pork, then slice it thickly while it is still warm.
Toss shredded daikon with gochugaru, fish sauce and sugar into a quick crunchy radish kimchi.
Wrap each slice in a salted cabbage leaf with the radish, raw garlic and a dab of salted shrimp.

recipes.name: Jjajangmyeon
steps: Fry the chunjang in plenty of oil for a few minutes to take off its raw bitterness, then set it aside.
Brown the diced pork belly and add the onion, potato and courgette until softened.
Stir the fried paste back in with a little water and simmer until glossy, then thicken with a cornflour slurry.
Ladle over just-boiled noodles and top with matchsticks of raw cucumber.

recipes.name: Kongguksu
steps: Soak the soybeans overnight, then boil them for about twelve minutes until just cooked through.
Rub off the loose skins and blend the beans with cold water and toasted sesame into a thick, smooth milk.
Chill the soy broth hard and season it with salt only at the table.
Boil and rinse the thin noodles, pile them in a bowl, pour over the icy broth and top with cucumber.

recipes.name: Kare-Kare
steps: Simmer the oxtail for two to three hours until the meat gives way at the bone, keeping the broth.
Steep the annatto seeds in hot oil and strain the orange oil into the broth.
Stir in the peanut butter and toasted rice powder and cook until the sauce is thick and velvety.
Blanch the aubergine, long beans and bok choy in the sauce and serve with bagoong on the side.

recipes.name: Sisig
steps: Boil the pork cheek and ear with aromatics until tender, then grill over coals until the edges char.
Chop the grilled pork very fine along with seared chicken liver.
Fry the chopped pork with onion, chilli and soy on a screaming-hot cast iron plate.
Finish with calamansi juice and crack a raw egg over the sizzling meat to fold through at the table.

recipes.name: Laing
steps: Simmer the garlic, ginger and onion in thin coconut milk until fragrant.
Lay the dried taro leaves on top and resist stirring them, or the dish turns itchy on the tongue.
Cook covered for about thirty minutes until the leaves collapse into the milk.
Stir in thick coconut cream and whole chillies and reduce until the leaves are dark, oily and glossy.

recipes.name: Ginataang Gulay
steps: Sweat the garlic, onion and ginger in a little oil until soft and fragrant.
Pour in the coconut milk and bring it to a gentle simmer without letting it split.
Add the squash first and cook until it starts to soften and thicken the sauce.
Fold in the long beans, aubergine and chilli and simmer until everything is just tender.

recipes.name: Assam Laksa
steps: Poach the mackerel, then flake the flesh off the bones and keep the fish stock.
Blend the chillies, lemongrass, shallots and shrimp paste into a rempah and fry it in oil.
Return the stock with tamarind and sliced torch ginger flower and simmer twenty minutes for a sharp, sour broth.
Add the flaked fish, pour over thick rice noodles and top with mint, pineapple and raw onion.

recipes.name: Mee Goreng Mamak
steps: Fry the cubes of tofu and boiled potato until browned at the edges.
Push them aside and scramble the eggs into the same very hot wok.
Add chilli paste, ketchup and a splash of soy, then throw in the yellow noodles and toss hard so they catch.
Finish with bean sprouts, crushed peanuts and a wedge of lime.

recipes.name: Hokkien Mee
steps: Boil the prawn heads and shells with pork bones to make a deep, sweet stock.
Fry garlic, prawns and squid in a very hot wok, then push them aside and scramble the eggs.
Add both noodles and ladle in the prawn stock, letting it soak in and reduce until the noodles are wet but not soupy.
Finish with a squeeze of calamansi and a spoon of sambal belacan on the side.

recipes.name: Bak Kut Teh
steps: Blanch the pork ribs to clear the scum, then rinse them clean.
Bring fresh water to the boil with whole garlic bulbs and lightly crushed white peppercorns in a spice bag.
Add the ribs and simmer for at least ninety minutes until the meat pulls away from the bone.
Season with both soy sauces near the end and serve with rice, youtiao and cut chilli in soy.

recipes.name: Sayur Lodeh
steps: Grind shallots, garlic, candlenut, coriander seed and turmeric into a smooth paste.
Fry the paste with bruised galangal, lemongrass and salam leaf until the oil separates out.
Pour in the coconut milk and add the chayote and long beans with cubed tofu and tempeh.
Simmer gently, adding the cabbage last, until everything is tender and the milk has not split.

recipes.name: Soto Ayam
steps: Simmer the chicken with lemongrass, lime leaves and galangal until tender, then lift it out and shred the meat.
Grind turmeric, candlenut, garlic and shallots into a paste and fry until the oil separates out.
Stir the paste back into the golden broth and simmer twenty minutes.
Ladle over glass noodles with the shredded chicken, boiled egg, fried shallots and a squeeze of lime.

recipes.name: Tempe Orek
steps: Cut the tempeh into thin matchsticks and fry until deep brown and crisp.
Fry sliced shallots, garlic, chilli and bruised galangal in a spoon of the same oil.
Melt the palm sugar with kecap manis and a little tamarind water into a dark syrup.
Toss the fried tempeh through the syrup over high heat until every piece is lacquered and dry.

recipes.name: Cha Ca La Vong
steps: Marinate cubes of catfish in turmeric, pounded galangal, garlic and a splash of rice wine for a few hours.
Grill or pan-fry the fish in plenty of oil until the edges catch and the turmeric smells toasted.
Bring the pan to the table over a burner and pile in whole dill fronds and lengths of spring onion to wilt in the hot fat.
Eat with cold vermicelli, crushed peanuts and a fiercely pungent shrimp-paste dip.

recipes.name: Banh Xeo
steps: Whisk the rice flour, turmeric, coconut milk and water into a very thin batter and rest it an hour.
Sizzle the prawns and thin pork slices in a screaming-hot pan, then ladle in the batter and swirl it thin.
Pile bean sprouts on one half, cover and steam until the edges lift and crackle.
Fold into a half-moon and eat wrapped in lettuce and herbs, dipped in nuoc cham.

recipes.name: Ca Kho To
steps: Cook the sugar in a clay pot with a splash of water until it turns a dark, faintly bitter caramel.
Add the shallots, garlic and fish steaks and turn them so every side is coated in the caramel.
Pour in fish sauce, coconut water and plenty of cracked black pepper and bring to a simmer.
Cook uncovered for about half an hour, spooning the sauce over, until it is thick, mahogany and clinging.

recipes.name: Pad See Ew
steps: Get the wok smoking hot and sear the garlic and sliced chicken until coloured.
Push them aside, scramble the eggs, then add the separated wide noodles.
Splash in dark soy, oyster sauce and sugar and let the noodles catch and char in places without over-stirring.
Toss through the Chinese broccoli stems and leaves and serve with chilli vinegar on the side.

recipes.name: Gaeng Hung Lay
steps: Marinate chunks of pork belly in the hung lay powder with a pounded paste of dried chilli, lemongrass and shrimp paste.
Fry the pork until the outside seizes and the spices smell toasted.
Add water, tamarind and palm sugar and simmer very slowly for about an hour and a half.
Stir in a mound of shredded ginger, pickled garlic and peanuts in the last ten minutes.

recipes.name: Nam Tok Moo
steps: Grill a whole piece of pork neck over charcoal until charred outside and still faintly pink in the middle.
Rest it, then slice thinly across the grain while still warm.
Toss the warm slices with fish sauce, lime juice, chilli flakes and sliced shallot.
Finish with toasted rice powder, mint and spring onion just before serving.

recipes.name: Pad Pak Boong
steps: Cut the morning glory into finger lengths, keeping the stems and leaves in separate piles.
Pound the garlic and chilli roughly in a mortar.
Get the wok as hot as it will go, throw in the garlic and chilli for a few seconds, then all the greens at once.
Splash in yellow bean sauce, soy and sugar and toss for under a minute so the stems stay squeaky.

recipes.name: Shan Noodles
steps: Cook the minced chicken with chopped tomato, garlic, ginger and paprika until it reduces to a thick red sauce.
Toss the boiled rice noodles with garlic oil, soy and a little of the noodle water so they stay loose.
Spoon the tomato-chicken sauce over the noodles with crushed peanuts and toasted sesame.
Serve with pickled mustard greens and a small bowl of clear broth alongside.

recipes.name: Lahpet Thoke
steps: Rinse and drain the fermented tea leaves, then dress them with garlic oil and a squeeze of lime.
Fry the sliced garlic until golden and keep both the chips and the oil.
Pile shredded cabbage, chopped tomato, peanuts, fried broad beans and sesame in mounds around the tea leaves.
Toss everything together at the table with salt and more lime, so the crunch stays intact.

recipes.name: Fish Amok
steps: Pound lemongrass, galangal, turmeric, kaffir lime zest and garlic into a fine kroeung paste.
Beat the paste with coconut cream, egg, fish sauce and palm sugar into a smooth custard base.
Fold in the cubed fish and spoon it into banana leaf cups lined with the leafy greens.
Steam the filled cups for about twenty-five minutes until the mousse is just set and springy.

recipes.name: Khao Piak Sen
steps: Simmer the chicken with ginger and garlic for an hour, then shred the meat and keep the broth.
Knead rice flour and tapioca starch with hot water into a soft dough and rest it under a cloth.
Roll the dough thin, cut it into thick noodles, and boil them straight in the broth so the starch thickens it.
Serve with the shredded chicken, fried garlic, spring onion, coriander and a wedge of lime.

recipes.name: Aloo Tama
steps: Soak and boil the black-eyed peas until they are almost tender.
Rinse the fermented bamboo shoots and fry them with turmeric until the sourness mellows.
Add cubed potato with ginger, garlic and cumin and fry for a few minutes.
Pour in water with the peas and simmer until the potato breaks slightly and the stew turns thick and sour.

recipes.name: Shabhaley
steps: Make a soft dough with the flour, a little salt and warm water, and rest it under a cloth.
Mix the minced beef with finely chopped cabbage, onion, ginger, garlic and chilli.
Roll rounds of dough, fill each with the mixture and crimp the edge into a sealed flat pastry.
Shallow-fry in a couple of centimetres of oil until both sides are blistered and deep golden.

recipes.name: Ambul Thiyal
steps: Soak the dried goraka in hot water and grind it into a black paste.
Rub the fish cubes with the goraka paste, pepper, chilli and salt and let them sit for half an hour.
Layer the fish in a clay pot with curry leaves, pandan, garlic and cinnamon and barely cover with water.
Cook uncovered over a low flame until the liquid has all but gone and the fish is coated in a near-black glaze.

recipes.name: Sri Lankan Cashew Curry
steps: Soak the raw cashews for a few hours until they swell and soften.
Simmer them in thin coconut milk with turmeric, curry powder, pandan and curry leaves until tender.
Temper sliced onion, green chilli and fenugreek in coconut oil and stir the tempering into the pot.
Finish with thick coconut milk and cook gently, never letting it boil, until the gravy is pale gold and thick.

recipes.name: Sauerbraten
steps: Marinate the beef for two to three days in vinegar, water, sliced onion, carrot, bay and cloves, turning it daily.
Pat the meat dry, sear it hard in a heavy pot until browned on all sides, then lift it out.
Strain the marinade into the pot, return the beef, cover and braise gently for about two and a half hours until fork-tender.
Crush the gingersnaps into the strained cooking liquid and simmer until the gravy thickens and turns glossy.
Slice the beef across the grain and spoon the sweet-sour gravy over it.

recipes.name: Semmelknödel with Mushroom Sauce
steps: Cube the stale rolls, pour over warm milk and leave twenty minutes until the bread is soft but not sludgy.
Work in the eggs, fried onion, parsley, salt and nutmeg until the mixture just holds when squeezed.
Shape wet hands into smooth balls and poach them in barely simmering salted water for eighteen minutes, never boiling.
Fry the sliced mushrooms hard in butter until browned, then add cream and a splash of stock and reduce to a coating sauce.
Lift the dumplings out to drain, halve them and spoon the mushroom cream over.

recipes.name: Kartoffelpuffer with Apple Sauce
steps: Grate the potatoes and onion coarsely, then squeeze out as much liquid as you can in a cloth.
Mix in the eggs, flour and salt and use the batter at once before it darkens.
Fry thin spoonfuls in hot oil, pressing them flat, until both sides are lacy and deep golden.
Simmer peeled chopped apple with a splash of water and a little lemon until it collapses into a coarse sauce.
Drain the pancakes on paper and serve hot with the warm apple sauce alongside.

recipes.name: Königsberger Klopse
steps: Mash the soaked bread with the mince, finely chopped anchovy, egg, grated onion and plenty of white pepper.
Roll the mixture into large smooth balls and poach them gently in salted stock for about fifteen minutes.
Make a pale roux with butter and flour, then whisk in the poaching stock to a smooth velvety sauce.
Stir in the capers, cream and a good squeeze of lemon so the sauce turns sharp and glossy.
Return the klopse to the sauce to warm through and serve with boiled potatoes.

recipes.name: Cottage Pie
steps: Brown the mince hard in a wide pan, then add diced onion and carrot and soften them in the fat.
Stir in tomato puree, Worcestershire sauce and stock and simmer twenty-five minutes until thick, not soupy.
Boil the potatoes and mash them with butter and warm milk until smooth and pipeable.
Spread the mince in a dish, cover with the mash and rake the top with a fork so it crisps.
Bake at 200C for twenty-five minutes until the peaks are browned and the edges bubble.

recipes.name: Steak and Ale Pie
steps: Toss the diced steak in seasoned flour and brown it in batches so it colours rather than steams.
Soften the onions, return the beef, pour in the ale and enough stock to cover, and simmer covered for ninety minutes.
Add the quartered mushrooms for the last twenty minutes and let the gravy reduce until it coats a spoon.
Cool the filling, tip it into a pie dish, lay the pastry over and crimp the edges firmly.
Brush with beaten egg, cut a steam vent and bake at 200C for thirty minutes until deep golden.

recipes.name: Cauliflower Cheese
steps: Break the cauliflower into florets and boil them for five minutes so they are just tender, then drain very well.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour and cook the roux for a minute before whisking in the milk a little at a time.
Simmer the sauce until it thickens, then take it off the heat and beat in most of the cheese and the mustard.
Fold the florets through the sauce, tip into a baking dish and scatter the remaining cheese on top.
Bake at 200C for twenty minutes until blistered and browned in patches.

recipes.name: Cullen Skink
steps: Poach the haddock gently in the milk for five minutes, then lift it out, flake it and keep the milk.
Sweat the chopped onion in butter without colouring, then add the diced potato and the reserved milk.
Simmer until the potato is soft, then crush some of it against the side of the pan to thicken the soup.
Return the flaked fish, warm through without boiling and season with plenty of black pepper.
Finish with chopped chives and a knob of butter melting on the surface.

recipes.name: Colcannon
steps: Boil the potatoes whole in their skins so they stay dry, then peel and mash them while hot.
Wilt the shredded kale in a little salted water for three minutes and drain it hard.
Warm the milk with the chopped spring onions so they soften and flavour it.
Beat the milk and half the butter into the mash, then fold the kale through in green ribbons.
Serve in a mound with a well of melted butter in the centre.

recipes.name: Gemista
steps: Slice the tops off the tomatoes and peppers as lids, scoop out the tomato flesh and blitz it to a pulp.
Fry the chopped onion in olive oil, stir in the raw rice, herbs and half the tomato pulp and cook two minutes.
Fill the vegetables two-thirds full with the rice mixture, since the rice will swell, and replace the lids.
Wedge potato chunks between them in the tray, pour over the remaining pulp with oil and a cup of water.
Bake at 180C for an hour and a quarter until the rice is soft and the tops are scorched, then rest before eating.

recipes.name: Briam
steps: Slice all the vegetables to the same thickness so they cook evenly in one tray.
Toss them with olive oil, oregano, salt and grated tomato until everything is coated.
Spread in a single crowded layer and add a splash of water to the tray.
Roast at 190C for an hour, turning once, until the edges caramelise and the liquid has almost gone.
Let it sit for ten minutes so the oil and juices settle, and eat warm with bread.

recipes.name: Pastitsio
steps: Simmer the mince with onion, passata, cinnamon and a little red wine for forty minutes until thick and glossy.
Boil the pasta until just under done, drain and toss it with a little of the grated cheese and beaten egg white.
Make a thick bechamel with butter, flour and milk, then beat in egg yolks and most of the cheese off the heat.
Layer pasta, then the meat sauce, then the remaining pasta, and pour the bechamel over to the corners.
Bake at 180C for forty-five minutes until the top sets golden, and rest thirty minutes before cutting.

recipes.name: Lamb Kleftiko
steps: Stab the lamb all over and push slivers of garlic deep into the cuts.
Rub it hard with lemon juice, olive oil, oregano, salt and pepper and leave it an hour.
Sit the lamb on a bed of potato wedges, wrap the whole lot tightly in parchment and then foil so no steam escapes.
Roast at 160C for three hours until the meat pulls away from the bone.
Open the parcel, raise the heat to 220C for fifteen minutes to colour the top, and serve in the juices.

recipes.name: Imam Bayildi
steps: Peel the aubergines in stripes, salt them for twenty minutes and pat dry to draw out bitterness.
Shallow fry them whole in olive oil until collapsed and bronzed, then set aside to cool.
Cook sliced onion and garlic slowly in the same oil until sweet, add chopped tomato and parsley and reduce.
Split each aubergine lengthways without cutting through and pack the onion filling into the pocket.
Add a little water to the pan, cover and bake at 180C for thirty minutes, then serve at room temperature.

recipes.name: Mercimek Corbasi
steps: Soften the chopped onion and carrot in a little oil, then stir in the tomato paste for a minute.
Add the rinsed red lentils and a litre of water and simmer thirty minutes until everything falls apart.
Blend the soup completely smooth and loosen with hot water to a pourable consistency.
Sizzle dried mint and pul biber in melted butter until the butter turns red and fragrant.
Ladle the soup out, trail the mint butter over it and serve with lemon wedges.

recipes.name: Karniyarik
steps: Stripe-peel the aubergines and fry them whole until the flesh softens, then drain on paper.
Fry the mince with onion until the water has gone and the meat starts to catch, then add chopped tomato, parsley and salt.
Slit each aubergine open and stuff it generously with the hot mince mixture.
Lay a tomato slice and a slit green chilli on each, sit them in a tray with a cup of tomato water.
Bake at 190C for thirty minutes until the tops blister and the sauce thickens around them.

recipes.name: Pisto Manchego
steps: Dice every vegetable to the same small size so the finished stew is uniform.
Cook the onion and peppers in olive oil over low heat for twenty minutes until sweet and slumped.
Add the courgette and cook another ten minutes without letting anything brown.
Stir in the grated tomato and bay and simmer uncovered until the liquid has reduced to a jammy sauce.
Season, rest off the heat for ten minutes and serve warm with bread or a fried egg on top.

recipes.name: Espinacas con Garbanzos
steps: Fry the bread and garlic in olive oil until crisp, then pound them with cumin and vinegar into a rough paste.
Wilt the spinach in the same pan in batches and drain off any water.
Add the chickpeas and smoked paprika and stir until everything is coated and fragrant.
Loosen with a splash of water, stir in the bread paste and simmer five minutes until it thickens around the chickpeas.
Check for salt and acidity and serve hot with more bread.

recipes.name: Bacalhau a Bras
steps: Cut the potatoes into matchsticks and fry them in hot oil until golden and crisp, then drain and salt.
Soften the sliced onion and garlic in olive oil, then add the flaked soaked salt cod and warm it through.
Fold the crisp potato straws into the fish so they stay separate.
Pour in the beaten eggs over low heat and stir constantly for a minute so they set creamy, never dry.
Kill the heat, scatter with parsley and olives and serve immediately.

recipes.name: Bouillabaisse
steps: Sweat sliced fennel, leek and onion in olive oil, then add tomato, orange peel, saffron and fish bones with water.
Simmer the broth forty minutes, then strain it hard, pressing everything through to get a full-bodied base.
Bring the broth back to a bare simmer and poach the firm fish first, adding the shellfish for the last four minutes.
Blend some broth with garlic, chilli, breadcrumbs and olive oil to make a thick rouille.
Serve the fish in wide bowls with broth ladled over and toasted baguette spread with rouille.

recipes.name: Gratin Dauphinois
steps: Rub a baking dish with a cut garlic clove and butter it well.
Slice the potatoes about three millimetres thick and do not rinse them, the starch is what thickens the gratin.
Warm the milk, cream, garlic, salt and nutmeg and simmer the slices in it for eight minutes.
Tip everything into the dish, level the top layer neatly and press the potatoes under the cream.
Bake at 160C for an hour until a knife slides through and the surface is deep gold, then rest fifteen minutes.

recipes.name: Poulet Basquaise
steps: Brown the seasoned chicken pieces skin-side down in olive oil until the skin is crisp, then remove them.
Cook the sliced peppers, onion and diced ham slowly in the same pan until soft and sweet.
Add the chopped tomato and piment d'Espelette and cook down to a thick pepper base.
Deglaze with white wine, sit the chicken back in skin-side up and simmer covered for thirty-five minutes.
Uncover for the last ten minutes so the sauce tightens and the skin crisps again.

recipes.name: Piperade
steps: Cook thinly sliced peppers, onion and garlic in olive oil over low heat for twenty minutes until melting.
Add chopped tomato and the piment and reduce until the mixture is thick and no longer watery.
Beat the eggs lightly and pour them into the pan over very low heat.
Stir slowly with a wooden spoon so the eggs set in soft curds through the peppers, and stop while still glossy.
Season and serve straight from the pan with crusty bread.

recipes.name: Cacio e Pepe
steps: Boil the pasta in less water than usual so the water turns properly starchy.
Toast the coarsely cracked peppercorns in a dry pan until they smell sharp, then add a ladle of pasta water.
Grate the pecorino very finely and whisk it with a little cooled pasta water into a smooth paste.
Drain the pasta while very al dente, toss it in the peppery pan, then take the pan off the heat.
Beat in the cheese paste off the heat, adding pasta water until the sauce turns creamy and clings without splitting.

recipes.name: Pasta alla Norma
steps: Salt cubed aubergine for half an hour, dry it well and fry in hot oil until deep brown and collapsed.
Sizzle sliced garlic in olive oil, add the tomatoes and a torn basil sprig and simmer twenty minutes into a thick sauce.
Cook the rigatoni al dente and drain it, keeping a mug of the water.
Toss the pasta through the sauce with most of the fried aubergine and a splash of pasta water.
Finish with the remaining aubergine, torn basil and a heavy grating of ricotta salata.

recipes.name: Ribollita
steps: Build a soffritto of finely chopped onion, carrot and celery in olive oil and cook it fifteen minutes until sweet.
Add the tomatoes, shredded cavolo nero and half the beans with plenty of water and simmer forty minutes.
Blend the rest of the beans smooth and stir them in to thicken the soup.
Tear in the stale bread, take the pan off the heat and let it stand until the bread dissolves.
Reheat the next day, which is what the name means, and serve with a heavy pour of raw olive oil.

recipes.name: Bigos
steps: Soak the dried mushrooms in hot water and keep the dark soaking liquid.
Brown the diced pork and sliced kielbasa hard so they render and colour, then set aside.
Cook the shredded fresh cabbage with onion in the fat until it wilts, then add the rinsed sauerkraut.
Return the meats with mushrooms, their liquid, prunes, juniper and bay and simmer very gently for two hours.
Cool the pot overnight and reheat the next day, when the stew is darker and far better.

recipes.name: Chicken Paprikash
steps: Cook the finely chopped onion slowly in lard until soft and pale gold, which takes at least fifteen minutes.
Pull the pan off the heat before stirring in the paprika so it never scorches and turns bitter.
Return to low heat, add the chicken, chopped tomato and pepper and a splash of water, then cover and stew forty minutes.
Whisk the flour into the sour cream, temper it with hot sauce, then stir it back in off the boil.
Warm through without boiling so the sauce stays smooth, and serve with nokedli or buttered noodles.

recipes.name: Khachapuri Adjaruli
steps: Knead a soft yeasted dough with flour, warm milk, yeast, a little sugar and salt and prove it for an hour.
Roll each portion into an oval, roll the long edges inwards and pinch the ends to form a boat.
Fill the hollow with the grated sulguni and crumbled feta, mounding it high.
Bake at 250C for twelve minutes until the crust is blistered and the cheese bubbles.
Pull the tray out, crack an egg into each molten centre with a knob of butter, return for two minutes and stir it in at the table.

recipes.name: Janssons Frestelse
steps: Cut the peeled potatoes into thin matchsticks and rinse them briefly so the gratin does not turn gluey.
Soften the thinly sliced onion in butter without letting it colour.
Layer potato, onion and the sprat fillets in a buttered dish, finishing with potato on top.
Pour over half the cream mixed with a little of the tin's brine, dot with butter and scatter breadcrumbs.
Bake at 200C for forty-five minutes, adding the rest of the cream halfway, until the top is bronzed and the potato is soft.

recipes.name: Stamppot
steps: Boil the peeled potatoes in salted water, laying the finely shredded kale on top for the last eight minutes.
Fry the sliced onion in butter until soft and just browning at the edges.
Drain the pot well, then mash the potato and kale together roughly so green streaks remain.
Beat in the warm milk, butter and mustard and season hard with salt and pepper.
Fold the fried onion through and serve mounded with a well of melted butter.

recipes.name: Mujadara
steps: Fry the thinly sliced onions in plenty of oil, patiently, until half are deep mahogany and crisp.
Boil the lentils with the cinnamon stick until almost tender but not split, then drain and keep the liquid.
Stir the rice, cumin and half the fried onion into the lentils with the measured cooking liquid.
Cover and steam on the lowest heat for eighteen minutes, then rest ten minutes without lifting the lid.
Fork it through, pile the remaining crisp onions on top and serve with yogurt or a cucumber salad.

recipes.name: Fesenjan
steps: Toast the walnuts lightly, then grind them to a fine damp paste in a processor.
Brown the chicken with sliced onion and turmeric until coloured, then set the chicken aside.
Cook the walnut paste in the pan with water over low heat for forty minutes, stirring, until the oil separates and the mixture darkens.
Stir in the pomegranate molasses and sugar, return the chicken and simmer another forty minutes until the stew is almost black.
Balance the sweet and sour to taste and serve with plain steamed basmati.

recipes.name: Kuku Sabzi
steps: Chop the herbs and spring onion as finely as you can, the mixture should be more green than egg.
Beat the eggs with turmeric, salt, pepper and a pinch of baking powder for lift.
Fold in the herbs, chopped walnuts and barberries so the batter is only just held together.
Pour into a well-oiled pan on low heat, cover and cook fifteen minutes until set underneath.
Flip it in one piece or finish under a grill, then cut into wedges and serve warm or cold with flatbread.

recipes.name: Koshari
steps: Fry the sliced onions in deep oil until dark and crisp and drain them on paper for the topping.
Boil the lentils until just tender, then cook the rice with a little of the onion oil and combine the two.
Boil the macaroni separately and keep it aside so nothing turns to mush.
Simmer the passata with garlic, chilli, cumin and vinegar into a sharp red sauce, and make a garlicky vinegar daqqa alongside.
Layer rice and lentils, macaroni, chickpeas and crisp onions in a bowl and let each person pour over sauce and daqqa.

recipes.name: Bissara
steps: Soak the split fava beans overnight, then drain and rinse them well.
Simmer them with whole garlic cloves and salt in plenty of water for about forty-five minutes until completely soft.
Blend to a thick smooth puree, adding cooking water until it pours slowly off the spoon.
Stir in cumin, olive oil and lemon juice and check the salt.
Serve very hot in bowls with a dusting of paprika, more olive oil and bread for dipping.

recipes.name: Gomen Wat
steps: Boil the shredded collards for ten minutes until they lose their raw edge, then drain and squeeze them.
Cook the chopped onion dry in the pan for five minutes before adding oil, the Ethiopian way of building sweetness.
Add crushed garlic, ginger, slit green chillies and turmeric and fry until fragrant.
Fold in the greens with a splash of water, cover and stew twenty minutes until silky and dark.
Season with salt and a squeeze of lemon and serve as part of an injera platter.

recipes.name: Yekik Alicha
steps: Rinse the split peas and boil them in unsalted water until they collapse, about thirty-five minutes.
Meanwhile cook the finely chopped onion dry over medium heat until it softens and gives up its water.
Add the oil, garlic, ginger and turmeric and fry into a pale gold base without letting it brown.
